title: Redesign: pick a design for each part

steps.headline: Which card layout should group pages use on a computer?

variants.label: Keep today's
variants.summary: What the combined branch looks like now, for comparison.

variants.label: Picture cards, 3 across
variants.summary: Like today but tidier: stars first, Easy setup a normal tag, family as one grey line, an (i) explains why it is listed there.

variants.label: Picture-left, 2 columns
variants.summary: Smaller picture on the left, two cards per row; family becomes a chip that opens a pop-up. Designer's pick.

variants.label: One column of rows
variants.summary: A list of wide rows, small picture, more text per line; easiest to scan top to bottom.

steps.notice: All three put stars first and make Easy setup a normal tag you can tap for its meaning.

steps.headline: Which card layout should group pages use on a phone?

variants.label: Keep today's
variants.summary: What the combined branch looks like now, for comparison.

variants.label: Rows with picture
variants.summary: Short rows with a small picture and one line of description.

variants.label: Rows with picture, family chip
variants.summary: Same rows; the family shows as a chip.

variants.label: Rows without picture
variants.summary: Drops the picture: about 5½ projects per screen instead of 1½ today.

steps.notice: Chip rows no longer wrap: they scroll sideways, as the design guide says.

steps.headline: Which project page top and family layout?

variants.label: Keep today's
variants.summary: What the combined branch looks like now, for comparison.

variants.label: Family card
variants.summary: A compact Family card under the top card: a mini list with status and an (i) for why and source. Designer's pick.

variants.label: Family chips
variants.summary: Family as chips ("4 forks") in the chip row; a pop-up holds the list with why and source.

variants.label: Sideways family cards
variants.summary: A sideways row of small family cards, this project outlined.

steps.notice: All three put the three link buttons back at the right of the top card, where they were.

steps.headline: Which search results layout on a computer?

variants.label: Keep today's
variants.summary: What the combined branch looks like now, for comparison.

variants.label: One card per result
variants.summary: A raised card with a picture; kind, match and devices in one sideways chip row.

variants.summary: Simple rows with the match strength at the right. Designer's pick on computers.

steps.headline: Which Most requested layout?

variants.label: Keep today's

variants.label: Ranked rows

steps.path: Tag my project → writing your pitch
steps.headline: Which Tag my project layout?

variants.label: Keep today's
variants.summary: What the combined branch looks like now, for comparison.

variants.label: One card per step
variants.summary: One narrow card per step; optional writing folds; Send says what is still missing and who will read it.

variants.label: With a live preview
variants.summary: The same card beside "How it will read", so you see the result as you write. Designer's pick.

variants.label: All steps folding
variants.summary: All four steps as folding rows on one page, finished steps summarised.

steps.headline: Where should "Managed by r/TrueOpenSource, drafted with AI help: claim this page" go?

variants.label: Grey line in the top card
variants.summary: One quiet line in the project's top card with "Are you the developer?" and a Claim button; nothing on cards. Designer's pick.

variants.label: "Unclaimed" chip
variants.summary: A dashed "Unclaimed" chip on cards and on the page, opening the explainer.

variants.label: Notice box
variants.summary: A tinted notice box on the project page with Claim this page inside it.

steps.notice: The label disappears once a developer claims the page.
